findings.title: Device is cached before database limit check, allowing device limit bypass on second request
findings.body: In `tagDeviceUI`, `a.localCache.SetDefault(key, struct{}{})` (line 87) is executed before calling `a.anonStore.CreateOrUpdateDevice(ctx, device)` (line 93). When the anonymous device limit has been reached, `CreateOrUpdateDevice` returns `ErrDeviceLimitReached` and the first request from a new device fails authentication as intended. However, because the device's cache key was already written to `localCache` with a 29-minute TTL, any subsequent request with the same `X-Grafana-Device-Id` header hits the cache at line 83 (`if _, ok := a.localCache.Get(key); ok { return nil }`) and bypasses `CreateOrUpdateDevice` entirely, succeeding authentication despite exceeding the device limit. `a.localCache.SetDefault` should only be called after `a.anonStore.CreateOrUpdateDevice` succeeds.

findings.title: Wire dependency injection broken after changing ProvideAnonymousDeviceService signature
findings.body: `ProvideAnonymousDeviceService` was changed to accept `sqlStore db.DB` instead of `anonStore anonstore.AnonStore`, and `anonstore.ProvideAnonDBStore` was changed to require `deviceLimit int64`, but `pkg/server/wire.go` and the generated `wire_gen.go` files were not updated in this PR. Because `wire.go` wires `anonstore.ProvideAnonDBStore` and `anonimpl.ProvideAnonymousDeviceService`, the server package will fail to compile or fail `make gen-go` until the wire providers and generated files are updated.

findings.title: MySQL RowsAffected() returns 0 when column values are unchanged, falsely triggering ErrDeviceLimitReached
findings.body: In `updateDevice`, `result.RowsAffected()` is checked for `0` to determine whether the device matched an active row within the expiration window. In MySQL (when `clientFoundRows=false`, the default in `go-sql-driver/mysql`), `UPDATE` returns `0` rows affected if a matching row is found but the new values (`client_ip`, `user_agent`, `updated_at`) are identical to the existing column values. Because MySQL `DATETIME` columns or fast repeat calls within the same second can have identical timestamps, a valid existing device can receive `rowsAffected == 0` and be rejected with `ErrDeviceLimitReached`.

findings.title: auth.anonymous settings ignore environment variable overrides
findings.body: `readAuthSettings` reads `iniFile.Section("auth.anonymous")` directly instead of `cfg.SectionWithEnvOverrides("auth.anonymous")`. As a result, `GF_AUTH_ANONYMOUS_DEVICE_LIMIT` (and the other keys in that section) will not work via environment variables unless `SectionWithEnvOverrides` is used.
